payload.statement_nl: For every real number x, floor(x) ≤ x.

result_payload.addressed_previous_feedback: The prior feedback indicated the proof was correct; I retained the same argument and stated explicitly that the conclusion follows immediately from the defining property of the floor function.
result_payload.proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By definition, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. In particular, floor(x) itself is an integer that is less than or equal to x. Therefore floor(x) ≤ x. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real number x.
result_payload.proof_summary: This follows directly from the defining property of the floor function: floor(x) is the greatest integer not exceeding x, hence it is always ≤ x.
